assetReads.description: Seated adult cradles a newborn across both arms, one hand supporting the head; their faces are turned toward each other and the setting contains only a mat.
Standing adult supports an awake baby at the lower body and upper back, holding the baby close with faces turned toward each other.
Adult sits on a mat with open hands beside the face; an awake baby lies on the front with forearms on the mat and looks toward the adult.
Child sits beside a basket holding one shoe while an adult kneels nearby, palm open, without taking the child’s hand.
Child stands on the floor using a small squeegee on a low window; adult kneels alongside using a cloth, with a small spray bottle on the floor.
Cropped view of bent child’s legs and a socked foot entering a shoe while the adult holds the shoe’s back tab.

decisions.assessment: Supported newborn holding and unforced face-to-face attention fit all three openings; the quiet-pause caption keeps the reading and movement contexts from implying a required response or technique.

The awake baby is held close with body and upper-back support, and the warm mutual attention remains an illustrative shared moment across looking, movement and conversation without a performance demand.
The adult’s open hands invite shared surprise while the baby rests freely on the mat; all three contexts retain pauses and responsive connection without requiring a posture, word or gesture.
The child holds the shoe while the nearby adult offers an open hand, preserving a small voluntary part in ordinary life across the shoe, pouring and drawing openings.

The child uses the squeegee from the floor beside an adult sharing the work, and the caption and three openings preserve supported participation without requiring a finished result or independent cleaning.

The close view shows help at the shoe rather than control of the child’s limb; all three age contexts and the phone reader preserve changing help needs, partial participation and the adult’s gentle time boundary.
